newsitem.title: UK: Iraq attacks damage U.S. credibility, says Al Haig.
newsitem.headline: Iraq attacks damage U.S. credibility, says Al Haig.

text.p: Former U.S. secretary of state Alexander Haig on Friday condemned President Bill Clinton for ordering missile attacks against Iraq, saying the move would be extremely costly to Washington's international standing.

"I think it has been a major assault on America's credibility," Haig told BBC Radio after the attacks were launched to drive out Baghdad's forces from northern Iraq where Iraqi Kurds occupy a "safe haven" under U.N. protection.

"The portrayal of this as an American victory is wrong-headed and would be proven to be so in the very near future," said Haig, who served under former Republican President Ronald Reagan in the 1980s.
The United States also expanded a no-fly zone over southern Iraq which was established after the 1991 Gulf War to protect Shiite Moslems from Saddam Hussein's forces.
The U.S. attacks sparked strong opposition from Russia, China and France, which said its warplanes would not help police the expanded part of the southern no-fly zone.
"What we have done is gotten away with a phoney response which is cheap in the near term but which will be extremely costly to American credibility on the long term," said Haig.
Republican commentators say the main reason Clinton launched the attacks was to boost his popularity ahead of presidential elections in November.
